title: El Niño usually weakens the monsoon, but not always
sources: IMD, end-of-season press release, southwest monsoon 2019 (El Nino and positive IOD; June-September season)
IMD long range forecast, April 2026, as reported by Down To Earth (El Nino expected; positive IOD could offset)
Down To Earth, 'El Nino may disrupt monsoons' (1997: about 101% of LPA); Anantam IAS explainer on El Nino and La Nina

quiz.q: Which of these usually helps India's monsoon?
quiz.why: Right. La Niña, the cooling phase in the central and eastern Pacific, tends to strengthen the Indian monsoon.

steps.text: Can push back on El Niño

claims.claim: El Nino is anomalous warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific; La Nina is anomalous cooling in the same region
El Nino typically weakens the Indian monsoon; La Nina tends to strengthen it / is favourable
In 1997, one of the strongest El Ninos, monsoon rainfall was about normal (about 101% of LPA; +2%)
A positive Indian Ocean Dipole can offset El Nino's effect on the monsoon; IMD forecasts consider both ENSO and IOD
The southwest monsoon season is June to September

review_note: Mostly secondary sources; IMD's 2019 end-of-season press release confirms the June-September season and IMD's use of El Nino and IOD. The 1997 figure differs slightly between sources (101% of LPA vs +2%), so the video says 'about normal' and '~100%'. Left out: the 2026 outcome (sources give a 12-13% deficit; still settling), the Walker circulation mechanism, Eurasian snow cover. The 'warmer western Indian Ocean' gloss for positive IOD is from the Anantam explainer.
